units.title: Creation fingerprint + drift attribution map
units.scope: Creation fingerprint over every effective create-time facet after composition, plus an attribution map from a changed composed facet back to the PRE-COMPOSITION tree key path. Identity-bearing facets named by identity; indexed paths only where the schema has no identity, and then with a changed-entry count ('mounts[] (2 entries changed)'). Never a hash-only message. Comments and formatting do not change the fingerprint; canonical semantic values do; host interpolation resolves before fingerprint comparison, but low-entropy resolved values are NEVER raw-hashed: fingerprint the authored expression plus a launcher-keyed HMAC/digest of the resolved value so changes are detected without offline-guessing exposure. ARCHITECT CORRECTION (C1/C2): this unit consumes E2.1's effective render, so it depends_on E2.1 directly, not only transitively. The launcher-keyed HMAC key itself is generated once and stored as exactly one record in hosttrust (never per-environment, never duplicated elsewhere); `pix reset` invalidates/rotates that one record together with every acceptance record (extends F6's one-store invariant to the key).

units.title: pix run cutover to sbx env create + name-based sbx exec
units.scope: THE cutover. Add --env NAME (exact name, no prefix matching, writes nothing to config, model precedence --model > [models].main > pi default). Unknown --env exits non-zero, creates no sandbox, never falls back to the default. Launch = render effective -> sbx env create -> poll for a positively identified instance -> bind lease to instance id -> sbx exec -it <name> -- pi <exact invocation>. Attach only on a schema-verified running row + matching instance id + matching creation fingerprint + still-reviewed environment; any drift refuses, names drifted facets by canonical key path, and prints `pix rm NAME && pix run --env ENV` with no --name. Holder leases, keep markers, orphan sweep, unknown-fails-closed all preserved. ARCHITECT CORRECTION (C7): wires the `env forget`/`env show` seams to these new live-launch facts — `forget` on a currently-attached environment tears down the bound lease/instance before invalidating the acceptance record, and `show` renders real live-holder/drift/attach state from this unit's EffectiveMounts/instance data instead of the Wave C placeholder ('unknown ... lands with a later wave').

integration_rationale: Wave A first: highest uncertainty (unproven upstream contract). A1/A2/A3 failing here costs 7 units; failing in wave D costs 22.
E1.1 second: cheapest unit in the plan, and it removes a whole class of misdiagnosis from every later host-backed run.
E1.4 before the parsers: security-critical refactor done while the existing pack trust suite is still alive to act as its oracle.
Pure parsers and the counter next: zero blast radius, and they turn wave D into wiring over tested primitives.
Wave C verbs in read-only -> write -> refuse -> consistency-sweep order: nothing in wave C can lose a sandbox or a credential.
E2.5 last in its wave and alone: the single highest-risk merge, arriving as a small diff over pre-landed parts.
E2.8 only after E2.5 has run live: deleting the old path before the new one is proven removes the fallback.
Wave E interleaves with D at no cost (E3.2 is TypeScript-only).
E4.3 before E4.2 or pix setup's local-model flow loses its RAM/download/context facts.
Wave G last of the code waves: highest line count, lowest uncertainty, gated by E5.1's trust translation.
Wave H last: AC-39 and AC-40 assert on the finished surface, and AGENTS.md serialization is only tolerable once.

rollback_posture.rule: reverting E2.5 after E2.8 has landed leaves no launch path at all; E2.5 and E2.8 must land within one working session and the private work environment must be converted and run live before E2.8
